summary: Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held positions at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), as Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library, and at Baroda Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State University.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. After earning his Dr. phil. and Lic. theol. at Halle-Wittenberg, he became professor there and later at Humboldt University of Berlin, also serving the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under tutor Franz Joseph Lauth. In 1864, he became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Kiel, Berlin (PhD) under Albrecht Weber, and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and the University of Göttingen.

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Anton Boller. He worked as a librarian at the Laurentian Library and Biblioteca Marciana, and held professorships at the universities of Bologna, Pisa, and Padua.

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist. She studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the faculty of the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning a PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University and held a post at Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Dhaka and Oxford (PhD). He directed the Bangladesh National Museum (1962–1991) and held leadership roles at the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art, ICOM, and Independent University, Bangladesh.

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he served as professor and professor emeritus at Kyushu University, professor at Kumamoto University, and director of the Kyushu Historical Museum.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held academic posts at Minobusan College, Nihon Fukushi University, and Rissho University, eventually becoming president of Minobusan University (1998–2002).
Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Mahidol University under the supervision of Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He later served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (ca. 1908–1923) and professor at Otani University.

Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Eastern Cultural Institute and later served as professor emeritus at Otani University.

Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded the Philosophical Society of Japan and Toyo University, serving as its lecturer and manager.

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University and Rissho University, and served as president of Miyagi University of Education.
Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor and later professor emeritus at Hanazono University.
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Ryukoku University under the doctoral supervision of Esho Mikogami.

Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the Australian National University in 1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University in the 1980s.

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1981. He held academic posts at the University of Milan and the University of Bologna.
